title: Wanstead & Woodford
intro: A leafy village on the edge of Epping Forest, with the lakes and follies of a vanished great house and a Georgian church in its old grounds.

items.name: Wanstead Park
items.blurb: The remains of the landscape around Wanstead House, one of the grandest houses in England until it was pulled down in 1825: a chain of lakes, woods, the Temple and the ruined Grotto.
items.tip: The Temple is open some weekends with displays about the park's history.

items.name: Eagle Pond and Snaresbrook Crown Court
items.blurb: A forest pond across the road from Snaresbrook Crown Court, a Gothic building of 1843 built as an orphan asylum and set in parkland.
items.tip: Look across Eagle Pond for the classic view.

items.name: Knighton Wood and Woodford Green
items.blurb: Old woodland with a pond and rhododendrons, once private gardens, now part of Epping Forest near Woodford Green and its statue of Winston Churchill.
items.tip: Walk on to the Churchill statue on the green.

items.name: Wanstead Flats
items.blurb: The southern tip of Epping Forest: a wide sweep of grassland, ponds and football pitches with big skies over east London.
items.tip: Alexandra Lake is a good spot to watch the birds.

items.name: St Mary's Church, Wanstead
items.blurb: A Grade I listed Georgian church of 1790 in the old grounds of Wanstead House, with box pews and a great monument to Sir Josiah Child.
items.tip: The churchyard is a quiet shortcut to Wanstead Park.

items.name: Wanstead High Street and Christchurch Green
items.blurb: The village high street with independent shops, cafés and pubs, and a green with a Victorian church spire in the middle.
items.tip: Saturday mornings are busiest; there is a farmers' market on the green some weekends.
